hero.title: Discover Islam
hero.subtitle: A complete introduction to the faith of over 2 billion Muslims

basics.title: What is Islam?
basics.description: Islam is the final and complete revelation from Allah (God) to humanity. It means 'submission to the will of Allah' and is a religion of peace, mercy, and justice.

coreBeliefs.title: The Six Pillars of Iman (Faith)
items: Belief in Allah (The One and Only God)
Belief in the Revealed Books (Quran as final)
Belief in the Messengers (Muhammad ﷺ as final)
Belief in the Day of Judgment

shahada.title: The Shahada (Declaration of Faith)
shahada.arabic: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدًا رسول الله
shahada.transliteration: Ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah
shahada.translation: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah
shahada.explanation: The Shahada is the first pillar of Islam and the gateway to the faith. By sincerely reciting it with understanding and conviction, one becomes a Muslim.
shahada.reference: Sahih Muslim (via Riyad as-Salihin 412) - The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger... Allah will forbid the Fire from touching him' (or admit him to Paradise according to narrations).

allah.title: Who is Allah?
allah.description: Allah is the Arabic name for the One True God. He is the Creator, Sustainer, and Owner of all that exists. Islam emphasizes strict monotheism (Tawhid). To Allah belong the Most Beautiful Names (Asma ul-Husna).
allah.quranReference: Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent. (Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4)

asmaUlHusna.title: 99 Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma ul-Husna)
asmaUlHusna.description: Allah has 99 Beautiful Names. Learning and calling upon Him by these names is highly recommended. Here is the complete authentic list with meanings:

names.meaning: The King and Owner of Dominion
The Perfection and Giver of Peace
The Lord of Majesty and Honour

prophet.title: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
prophet.description: Muhammad ibn Abdullah (570-632 CE) is the final messenger sent by Allah to all humanity. He is the example of perfect character and conduct.
keyTeachings: Honesty and truthfulness in all dealings
Mercy to all creation, including animals
prophet.quranReference: And indeed, you are of a great moral character. (Surah Al-Qalam 68:4)
prophet.hadithReference: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'I have been sent to perfect good character.' (al-Muwatta 1614)

quran.title: The Holy Quran
quran.description: The Quran is the literal word of Allah revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over 23 years. It remains unchanged in its original Arabic text.
facts: No single letter has changed in 1,400 years
quran.reference: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Quran and indeed, We will be its guardian. (Surah Al-Hijr 15:9)

salah.title: Salah (The Five Daily Prayers)
salah.description: Salah is the second pillar of Islam and the most important act of worship after faith. It is performed five times daily at specific times.
benefits: Connects the believer directly to Allah
salah.reference: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. (Surah Al-Ankabut 29:45)

zakat.title: Zakat (Charity)
zakat.description: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam — a mandatory charity of 2.5% on qualifying wealth held for one lunar year above the nisab threshold. It purifies wealth and helps the poor.
eligibleRecipients: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled
zakat.reference: Zakah expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy... (Surah At-Tawbah 9:60)

sawm.title: Sawm (Fasting in Ramadan)
sawm.description: Fasting during the month of Ramadan is the fourth pillar of Islam. Muslims abstain from food, drink, and marital relations from dawn to sunset.
benefits: Empathy for the hungry and poor
sawm.reference: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous. (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183)

hajj.title: Hajj (Pilgrimage)
hajj.description: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam — obligatory once in a lifetime for those physically and financially able. It occurs annually in Mecca during Dhul-Hijjah.
hajj.reference: And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. (Surah Ali 'Imran 3:97)

afterlife.title: Belief in the Afterlife
afterlife.description: Muslims believe in life after death — the Day of Judgment when every soul will be held accountable for their deeds.
concepts: Resurrection of the body and soul
afterlife.reference: Every soul will taste death. And you will be paid in full your reward on the Day of Resurrection. (Surah Ali 'Imran 3:185)

dos: Establish the five daily prayers on time
Recite and reflect on the Quran daily
Give charity regularly, even a small amount
Be honest and truthful in all dealings
Respect parents and maintain family ties
Make Du'a (supplication) to Allah for all needs
Follow the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
donts: Shirk (Associating partners with Allah) — the greatest sin
Eating pork or improperly slaughtered meat
Gambling and all forms of usury (Riba)
Arrogance and looking down on others

faqs.question: How does one become a Muslim?
faqs.answer: To become a Muslim, one must sincerely recite the Shahada with full understanding and conviction.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Islam, Iman, and Ihsan?
faqs.answer: Islam refers to the outward actions (the 5 pillars). Iman refers to the inner beliefs (the 6 pillars of faith). Ihsan refers to worshipping Allah as if you see Him, knowing He sees you (Sahih Muslim 8).

faqs.question: Do Muslims worship the same God as other religions?
faqs.answer: Muslims worship Allah — the One and Only God. He has no partners, no children, and no equals (Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:1).

faqs.question: Why do Muslims pray five times a day?
faqs.answer: The five daily prayers were ordained during the Isra and Mi'raj. They provide spiritual discipline and connection to Allah (Surah Al-Ankabut 29:45).

faqs.question: What is the role of women in Islam?
faqs.answer: Islam elevated women’s status with rights to inheritance, education, and consent. Men and women are equal in spiritual reward. 'The best of you are those best to their women' (Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3895).

faqs.question: Are all Muslims Arab?
faqs.answer: No. Only about 20% of Muslims are Arab. The largest Muslim populations are in Indonesia, Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, and Nigeria.
